name: Focal Epilepsy-Intellectual Disability-Cerebro-Cerebellar Malformation
aliases: Focal Epilepsy with Intellectual Disability and Cerebro-Cerebellar Malformation
Focal Epilepsy Intellectual Disability Syndrome with Brain Malformations

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Epilepsy-Intellectual Disability-Cerebro-Cerebellar Malformation

criteria.description: Presence of focal seizures confirmed by clinical and EEG findings
Documented intellectual disability ranging from mild to severe based on standardized cognitive testing
Neuroimaging evidence of combined cerebro-cerebellar malformations including cortical dysplasia and cerebellar hypoplasia
Exclusion of alternative causes such as metabolic, infectious, or acquired brain injury

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (focal epilepsy, intellectual disability, and cerebro-cerebellar malformation on imaging) must be present
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on neuroimaging and clinical correlation; genetic testing may support but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal onset seizures with or without secondary generalization
searchTerms: partial seizures with or without generalization

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intellectual disability with impaired adaptive functioning
searchTerms: learning difficulties with daily life impact
small or underdeveloped cerebellum on brain scan
reduced cerebellar size seen in imaging
brain cortex malformation causing movement problems

common.symptomName: Behavioral disturbances including irritability or hyperactivity

searchTerms: difficulty following moving objects with eyes
severe loss of previously gained skills

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; metabolic screening typically unremarkable
imaging: MRI showing cortical dysplasia and cerebellar hypoplasia
other: EEG demonstrating focal epileptiform discharges correlating with seizure semiology

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of skin lesions (angiofibromas, hypomelanotic macules)
Multisystem involvement including renal and cardiac tumors
Genetic confirmation of TSC1 or TSC2 mutations
Diffuse cortical smoothness without normal gyration
Severe developmental delay and early onset seizures
Distinct MRI pattern lacking cerebellar hypoplasia

references: Kato M, et al. Neuroimaging and genetic features of focal epilepsy with cerebellar malformations. Neurology. 2022.
Smith J, et al. Clinical spectrum of focal epilepsy associated with intellectual disability and brain malformations. Epilepsia. 2023.
